gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: Can you ___ me on which course to choose?
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb (to give advice); 'advice' is the uncountable noun and 'advices' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
gaps.hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
gaps.explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.
'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: Please state your ___ on the application form.
gaps.hint: the formal word for your type of work, used on forms
gaps.explanation: 'Occupation' is the formal word for a person's job or profession, typically used on official forms.
